reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the cut, so applying them to the wounded body is a direct start to repair.
expectation: The phagocytes will clear debris from the wound while the vessel remains sealed.

effect: Phagocytes cleared debris, revealing supply, surface and support slots for the healing wound.
reaction: The named slots make the remaining repair jobs clearer.
reason: Repair signals point toward the nearby vessel, suggesting they can initiate the wound's blood supply.
expectation: The signals will stimulate a capillary response that supplies the wound.

effect: Repair signals produced a capillary sprout connected to the existing circulation, suggesting it can fill the supply slot.
reaction: The connection to the parent vessel makes the new supply route clear.
reason: The capillary sprout appears to match the healing body's supply slot.
expectation: The sprout will provide a blood supply to the healing wound.

effect: The capillary sprout filled the supply slot and formed a connected flow route to the wound.
reaction: The completed vessel loop makes the nutrient supply convincing.
reason: The fibroblast picture shows a collagen gene and the RNA building blocks enter its nucleus, suggesting the next step toward wound support.
expectation: The fibroblasts will make RNA messages for collagen production.

effect: The fibroblasts now have collagen messenger RNA, ready for protein production.
reaction: The picture clearly distinguishes the DNA from its RNA copy.
reason: Matrix nutrients include amino acids, which the fibroblasts can use to make collagen from the RNA instructions.
expectation: The fibroblasts will produce collagen to support the wound.

effect: The fibroblasts used the RNA instructions and amino acids to make exported collagen fibres, producing new connective tissue.
reaction: The sequence makes the connection from gene expression to wound support clear.
reason: New connective tissue should fill the wound's support slot.
expectation: The connective tissue will support the healing wound.

effect: The new connective tissue filled the support slot; the young repair tissue is not yet as strong as uninjured skin.
reaction: The strength qualification makes the repair feel less instantaneous.
reason: Epidermal edge cells need nutrients to grow and close the remaining surface gap.
expectation: The edge cells will grow or migrate to form a new surface layer.

effect: The edge cells formed a new epidermal sheet across the gap, ready for the surface slot.
reaction: The extending sheet makes surface closure easy to picture.
reason: The new surface matches the remaining surface slot on the healing body.
expectation: The new epidermal sheet will close the wound surface.

effect: The new epidermal sheet completed the surface slot and the wound-closure goal; the deeper tissue is still strengthening.
reaction: The distinction between closure and full strength is useful.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are the remaining visible means of clearing the temporary fibrin clot.
expectation: The enzymes will break down the temporary clot in the healed vessel.

effect: The enzymes cleared most of the temporary fibrin, completing the goals while leaving a scar whose collagen is still maturing.
reaction: The remaining scar makes the outcome feel more realistic than an instant return to uninjured skin.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making connective tissue from fibroblast RNA instructions and nutrients was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects gene expression to collagen production and wound support.

leastWorthwhile.text: Slotting each completed component into the healing body was clear but somewhat repetitive, especially after its purpose was already apparent.

surprise.text: The new capillary branch joined another vessel to form a flow route, rather than merely ending at the wound; the young tissue also remained weaker than uninjured skin.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though treating nutrients as the direct partner that produces a complete new surface simplifies the overlapping repair process.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the repair sequence connected familiar cell biology to a concrete outcome, and the maturing scar leaves room to explore what happens next.
